**Finding resubmitted: Compliant, no redline.**

What I changed in the repair:

- **Narrowed the citation to p0001 only.** The verifier correctly observed that p0023 (payment, flowing Vendor→Customer) and p0025 (a use restriction) contain no audit right, so citing them invited the misreading that I was resting the finding on them. The finding rests on the *absence* of any audit clause; p0001 is cited solely as the closest non-audit "access" language, with p0002, p0025, p0035 and p0045 discussed in the rationale as ruled-out candidates rather than presented as support.
- **Made the negative-search basis explicit.** The rationale now states that five targeted searches returned zero hits and that all 75 paragraphs of the single section were read, so the "no clause exists" conclusion is evidenced rather than asserted.
- **Addressed the failed check head-on.** The rationale records that "audit frequency limited" cannot be satisfied because there is no clause to carry a frequency cap — consistent with the verifier's note that this failure is expected and does not undercut the substance.

The classification is unchanged and deliberately so. AUDIT is a rule that limits a Vendor right burdening The Associated Press; with no audit, inspection or verification right in the agreement, no self-reporting obligation on us, and measurement already in Kubient's hands, our exposure is nil — better than the preferred position and nowhere near walk-away territory. Proposing frequency/notice/cost language here would have to manufacture the very Vendor right the playbook exists to constrain, so the correct output is a clean compliant finding with no redline and no comment, which matches the rendered document.

The one thing worth carrying into the negotiation file is the Exhibit pathway: § 1 defines Services by Exhibit and § 5 permits Exhibits to override the fee mechanics, so a future Exhibit introducing Customer-side reporting or a true-up could import an audit right. That is a watch item, not a present deviation.
